articles.title: GHSA: Nginx UI: Casdoor SSO callback uses a constant `state` parameter (login CSRF)
articles.summary:
## Summary

In the Casdoor SSO flow, the OAuth `state` parameter is hard-coded to `settings.CasdoorSettings.Application` — a value identical for every user and every login. The callback handler accepts whatever `state` the client sends without comparing it to anything stored in the user agent, enabling a login-CSRF: an attacker can force the victim's browser to authenticate as the *attacker*.

articles.title: GHSA: Nginx UI: Auto backup name allows path traversal outside validated storage path
articles.summary:
## Summary

Nginx UI validates `backup_path` and `storage_path` against the administrator-defined `backup.GrantedAccessPath` boundary, but the final auto-backup output filename is built from the user-controlled auto-backup `name` without stripping path separators or `..` components.

An authenticated user who can create or modify an auto-backup task can set a name such as `task/../../../escaped`.

articles.title: GHSA: Nginx UI: MCP configuration tools bypass restricted directive validation and allow secondary authenticated users to execute NJS in Nginx worker context
articles.summary:
